summary: Aru territory part 2 (Kakwa chefferie/Adi health zone around Ingbokolo, Adja, Laybo/Kaliko-Omi and Biringi/Ndo areas, northern Ituri on the Uganda and South Sudan borders) is outside the Ituri conflict core (CODECO in Djugu/Mahagi, ADF in Irumu/Mambasa) and no armed group holds territory. Towns (Ingbokolo, Gombe, Atsinia, Eriku, Mobiri, Laybo) are state-held with PNC, territorial administration and some FARDC; state forces are themselves accused of illegal roadblocks and extortion in Kakwa. Since late 2025 the South Sudan border strip of Kakwa (Rumu/Azu/Liku/Kongoroko groupements) and Kaliko-Omi has suffered repeated cross-border incursions by South Sudanese armed men (reported as SPLA-IO 'AIO' rebels and SSPDF soldiers): looting, killings and mass abductions (70+ at Ulendere/Arile, 11-12 May 2026), with preventive displacement and only a thin FARDC presence; these border villages are rated contested/low confidence. Rest of the rural area is state police by default; Mbororo herders reported in Ndo/Biringi in June 2026 were expelled. Reviewed 2026-10-01 with web research.

new_entities.name: SPLA-IO (Sudan People's Liberation Army in Opposition)
new_entities.description: South Sudanese armed opposition (Riek Machar's SPLM-IO); elements from Central Equatoria cross into Aru/Faradje (DRC) for looting and abductions; called 'AIO' locally.

new_entities.name: South Sudan People's Defence Forces
new_entities.description: National army of South Sudan; soldiers reported making cross-border incursions into Aru territory (Ituri) in 2025-2026.

zones.description: Main towns: Ingbokolo (Kakwa chefferie trading centre near Uganda border), Gombe, Atsinia, Eriku, Mobiri, Laybo
zones.evidence: Ingbokolo and the other towns host chefferie/territorial administration, PNC and state services (CNPR post reopened Aug 2026, Ebola prevention campaigns Aug 2026); no armed group holds them. Insecurity is criminal (armed robberies in Aru/Ariwara, July 2026) and state forces are accused of illegal roadblocks and extortion in Kakwa (Oct 2025), confirming state forces as the coercive power. South Sudanese incursions hit border villages, not these towns.

zones.description: Villages within ~9 km of the South Sudan border: Kakwa chefferie (Adi HZ: Azu, Rumu, Liku, Kongoroko, northern Gaki/Rikazu/Etukaliri health areas, e.g. Nyangbara, Ranyaka, Bazi, Kendrio, Leiko, Karagba, Nyeite) and Kaliko-Omi (Lipku)
zones.evidence: Since Dec 2025 repeated incursions by armed men from South Sudan (reported as SPLA-IO 'AIO' groups of 100+ and SSPDF soldiers) in Kakwa border groupements (Rumu, Agoroba, Ulendere, Arile) and Kaliko-Omi: looting of cattle, killings, sexual violence and abductions (70+ people 11-12 May 2026, per OCHA), causing preventive displacement into the bush. Raiders withdraw across the border and no foreign force is reported holding villages; local leaders say the FARDC presence on the border is 'very minimal'. Army assigned as main state force with low confidence; status contested because of recurrent raids.

zones.description: Rural villages of Kakwa (Adi) away from the South Sudan border, Adja, Laybo/Kaliko-Omi interior and Biringi/Ndo areas
zones.evidence: No reported armed-group control in these rural areas as of 2026; South Sudanese incursions concern the immediate border strip. Mbororo herders reported in Ndo secteur (Bholi, June 2026) were expelled by local authorities. Assigned to state police/customary authorities by default.
